newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says Communist Party newspaper a must.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says Communist Party newspaper a must.

text.p: Vietnam's Politburo has ordered all Communist Party cells, branches and mass organisations to buy and read Cong San and Nhan Dan, the official party magazine and daily newspaper, Nhan Dan itself said on Friday.
The announcement came just two days after the Nhan Dan broadsheet, faced with growing competition from a vast choice of more lively publications, doubled in size to eight pages a day.

Nhan Dan said the move was designed to "strengthen party leadership across the whole of society (and) deliver the voice of the party, state and people to officials, party members and people throughout the country".
It said party organisations should propagandise the daily and encourage party officials and members and people in general to buy and read the paper and write comments on its content.

Nhan Dan (The People), which celebrated the 45th anniversary of its first issue last year, currently has a daily circulation of around 170,000. The paper has pledged to liven up its columns in a bid to win the loyalty of readers who can now buy newspapers packed with human interest stories.

However, the Communist Party still sees Nhan Dan as its mouthpiece and often refers to its reporters as an army fighting for the politics and ideology of the country. Accordingly, it tends to paint a glowing picture of industrial, economic or diplomatic achievements.
The official Vietnam News Agency said on Friday that the party's membership increased by 91,452 in 1996, six percent more than in 1995.
It gave no figure for total membership, though most recent official figures put it at 2.128 million -- less than three percent of the population.
